title: An early time covariance reduces omitted-night error by 7.6 percent for GJ 3323, but block ranges include zero
abstract: We test whether an early time covariance predicts later omitted nights in a known GJ 3323 velocity extraction difference. An exponential covariance fitted to 55 early exposures reduces weighted squared error by 7.62 percent in 66 later exposures on 63 nights. Each prediction omits the full target night. Conditional 10-day and 30-day stability ranges are -1.22 to 17.53 percent and -2.61 to 20.43 percent. Both include zero. A within-season shuffle fraction is 0.0255 under pair exchangeability. The fitted time scale reaches every tested upper cap from 30 to 1000 days. Thus the point gain does not establish a stable correction or a finite physical lifetime. The products share spectra and can share template errors. No planet is confirmed or excluded, and no independent instrument observation is added. Original code, aggregate evidence, input hashes and separate-scratch reproduction steps are included. The external database is excluded.

display.caption: Later omitted-night gain with covariance frozen from the early season. Bars show conditional bin stability ranges. The right panel gives the conditional date-shuffle distribution. These tests use different assumptions; neither identifies a physical cause.
